commits.subject: Every dependency with a security advisory moved to its patched release

body.text: Clears all 17 open Dependabot alerts, and one pnpm audit found that Dependabot had not yet raised:

items: vite 8.2.0 to 8.3.5 (7 alerts, launch-editor and server.fs among them)
vitest and @vitest/mocker 4.1.11 to 4.1.12 (2)
undici 8.11.2 to 8.12.3, under jsdom (5)
source-map-js 1.2.1 to 1.2.2 (1)
@fastify/busboy 3.2.1 to 3.2.4, under @netlify/blobs (1)
tinypool 2.1.0 to 2.1.2 (2 critical), by an override: oxfmt pins it exactly, and a newer oxfmt is a formatter upgrade of its own
zod 4.6.6 to 4.6.7, under eslint-plugin-react-hooks

body.text: Every one is a patch or minor release inside the range already asked for; pnpm audit finds nothing after it.

commits.subject: Pausing neither dims the screen nor says Paused

body.text: While dwelling is switched off, the board is left exactly as it is: no Paused across the middle and nothing dimmed. Resume over the row of controls says it is off, and is still the way back.

commits.subject: A phrase said in auto-speak is saved as edit mode's Save saves it

body.text: Said on a category of somebody's own, a phrase Library has already is now filed under that tab too, as Save files words already on the board — typed out, chosen off the board after typing, or with its choices made. It filed only a message Library did not have, so a phrase found by typing on a tab and said was nowhere on that tab afterwards. One chosen off the tab it is on changes nothing, and no second copy is ever made.
Either is now a change Undo reaches, is pointed at, and is said in a toast where a tab took it — after "Copied to clipboard" for a copy.

commits.subject: No phrase cell skips its drawing on an iPad or iPhone

body.text: Safari on an iPad still lost the phrase under the pointer as it was magnified — the first few in a tab, every one from the home screen — with the magnified cell itself drawn. Off-screen skipping (content-visibility: auto) is now off for every cell on iOS WebKit, found by -webkit-touch-callout, which only iOS supports; the window of rendered cells keeps the grid light there. Elsewhere it stays.

commits.subject: The guide says which voices each browser offers, and how to install Peri on each device

body.text: Better voices: Chrome on a Mac lists every installed voice where Safari lists fewer; on an iPad or iPhone every browser offers the same shorter list, often without downloaded Enhanced voices; Siri and Personal Voice are never offered to a web page; and a voice one browser lacks is said in the default voice there, never in silence.

Using it offline: installing on an iPad or iPhone, in Chrome on a Mac or a PC, on a Chromebook and on Android — and that the home-screen app on an iPad keeps its own board apart from Safari, so a backup or Synchronize carries it across.

commits.subject: The device's voices are read again when the picker opens and Peri is looked at

body.text: iOS can add a voice — one downloaded in Settings while Peri waited in the background — without firing voiceschanged, and the list was read only when that fired. It is now read again whenever the voice picker opens and whenever Peri is looked at, which also refreshes the spoken languages. Voices iOS never offers web pages, Siri's and Personal Voice among them, are still out of reach.

commits.subject: A phrase the device voice never began is handed over again

body.text: Sometimes a phrase chosen went into the message box and nothing was heard. Every phrase begins by cancelling whatever was being said, and Chrome can drop what it is handed straight after a cancel; a synthesiser left paused takes the words and says nothing. Peri noticed the silence a second later and took it as the phrase having ended.

The synthesiser is now resumed before every phrase, and a phrase neither begun nor ended a second after it was handed over is handed over again, once, before its silence is believed. One that began is never repeated.

commits.subject: An open copy of Peri offers a newer version when one is out

body.text: Peri updated itself on every opening with a connection, but a copy already open ran the release it was opened on for as long as it stayed open. It now asks now and then whether the page names another script, and a strip at the top says a new version is ready: Update now reloads into it, Later waits until a newer one still. Never reloaded by itself, since a reload loses whatever is in the message box.

commits.subject: The magnified phrase is always drawn

body.text: On an iPad the phrase under the pointer vanished as it was magnified. A cell may skip its painting while the browser thinks it out of view, its size held to a placeholder while it does, and the magnified cell is moved out of its place and sized to its words — so Safari could take it as skipped and give its width as nothing. It is never skipped now; every other cell still is.

commits.subject: A phrase said for the first time is counted and shown where it went

body.text: A message said or copied was kept in Library and never seen: used once, it sat behind every phrase used more under Most used, below the first screen of a board in use, and read as not kept at all. The board now points at it — marked and scrolled to wherever the order puts it — once the words have ended and the box has stopped searching.

And a phrase said with edit mode's Speak and save was saved but never counted as used, so under Recently used it sat at the very end of the board; a question answered in edit mode is answered that way. It is counted now, the phrase Save made or the one that says the words where Save refused them, and pointed at the same way.

commits.subject: One pair of floating arrows for all scrolling, repeating on a click too

body.text: Every panel, picker and the sign-in page had a rail of four scroll controls; the two text boxes past their cap had small arrows of their own. All of them now have the grid's two floating arrows — up at the top of the right edge, down at the foot, translucent, a page of five sixths at a time, each only while there is somewhere to go.

A click on a scroll arrow now goes on paging while the pointer stays, as a rest does: an operating system's dwell-click is a click, and the arrows paged once for a gaze that went on resting on them. Only the arrows; a click on backspace or a spinner still acts once.

The down arrow rises clear of Peri's keyboard only where the keyboard is over it, which at its present size is never — it was lifted whatever, and stood in mid-air. And the keyboard steps aside while nothing on screen can be typed into, coming back by itself when something can.

commits.subject: The guide brought up to date

body.text: A read of every section against the app as it is: a phone's top row is the modes and the menu alone, with no clipboard or Undo; how to add an emergency phrase, and that one opens rather than speaks in edit mode with an empty box; dialogs that ignore the pointer until it moves and do not close when pressed outside; adding an emergency phrase on Undo's list; the panels' scroll arrows down their right edge; eleven word lists, not nine; how to reach edit mode; suggested answers kept as phrases when said while a question is open; and what stays on each device rather than synchronizing.

commits.subject: Peri's keyboard floats over the board, small and gold, beside present

body.text: The keyboard's button moves from the left of the message card to the end of the modes, right after present, lit while the keyboard is up.

The keyboard itself no longer takes the bottom of the screen with the board giving up that height. It floats over the phrase grid, translucent and framed in the brand's gold, standing on the emergency bar so that bar is never covered; the grid makes room under its last row for what it hides and lifts its down arrow above it. It is smaller: about a fifth of the screen high and no wider than 40% of it. Every key now fills as it is rested on, where a rest showed only a green edge.

commits.subject: Listen mode answers in edit mode, and every mode says it changed

body.text: Opening the question box turns auto-speak off: the board goes into edit mode, so an answer is built in the box out of phrases and suggested answers and said when it is ready, rather than each phrase said the moment it is chosen. A suggested answer chosen there goes in place of what the box held, the caret in its gap, and is recorded for the next question; a question that settles into an empty box still answers itself. Speak in edit mode saves as well, so an answer said is kept as a phrase.
Closing it goes back to the mode it opened from, the answer carried into the message box. Auto-speak's control, while a question is open, stops listening and turns auto-speak on.
Listen mode, please and the presentation window now say in a toast when they come on and go off, as auto-speak does — the window when it closes from its own side too.

commits.subject: The toast is a sleek pill

body.text: The toast was a light box framed in a ring of the accent 1.3rem thick, the whole at 85%, which read as a warning sign more than a line of news. It is a pill now: opaque, a hairline edge, a two-layer shadow, and a short rise and fade as it comes in, with none for somebody who has asked for less motion. Still the board turned inside out, a light ground and dark words, where a gaze working the board already is.

commits.subject: Each order in the order picker shows its glyph left of its name

body.text: The tiles in Order the phrases were words alone, while the control that opens them shows each order as a glyph. Each tile now draws that glyph before its name, so the tile and the control are learnt as one; the selected tile's glyph takes the tile's colour.

commits.subject: An emergency phrase is added from a plus after the bar, in every mode

body.text: The edit-mode tool at the end of the emergency bar opened a blank emergency draft in the message box, which looked exactly as it had, so nothing said the next Save would go to the bar and it read as doing nothing. It is gone. A bare plus now follows the last button in every mode, drawn as Add category is after the last tab and taking 1.75rem and a 0.75rem gap, and it opens a dialog for the words: the message box is left alone, words a button already says are refused, and the addition is on Undo's list.

The dialog is guarded against the press that opened it, said again: an operating system's dwell-click went on clicking where the plus had been, where a press on the screen round the dialog closed it, and the next opened it again. That screen closes nothing now, and nothing answers a rest or a click until the pointer is aimed somewhere new as the dialog comes and goes. Add category shares the dialog and the guard.

commits.subject: Undo and Redo for the board, and no clipboard controls on a phone

body.text: Saves, deletes, phrases taken out of a category and deleted categories can now be undone and done again, by Undo and Redo after Paste in the message card's top row, in both modes. Each names what it will reach. The last 50 changes are kept on this device across a reload, in no backup and nothing Synchronize sends; the words of deleted phrases are among them, which the guide and the privacy policy say. A change is kept as the difference it made and applied to the board as it stands, so what came since is left alone. This replaces the single undo that appeared after a delete.

On a phone, Copy, Paste, Undo and Redo are not drawn: the top line had no room for them, and the modes were squeezed into a column three deep. A delete on a phone is final; the phone's own copy and paste are a press on the box away.

commits.subject: A phrase found by typing in edit mode opens, and the board scrolls to it

body.text: In edit mode, a phrase found by typing into an otherwise empty box went in as words: a copy of itself with no cell to carry its tools, which Save then refused. Where it is on the tab showing it now opens, ready to be changed, and the board brings its cell into view and marks it once the search lets the tab back. After other words, or off the tab, it goes in at the caret as before.

Bringing a cell into view far down a long tab also landed a screen and a half past it: cells take their real height only as they near the screen, so the scroll's target moved while it ran. The grid now aims again once the scroll comes to rest, which also fixes it for a phrase just saved.

commits.subject: Auto-speak is the one mode button, lit while it is on

body.text: Edit and auto-speak were two buttons side by side, one of them always lit, so the board said which mode it was in twice. Now auto-speak is the only one: lit while it is on, and turning it off is edit mode, as it always was. The pencil is gone from the row, and the guide says to turn auto-speak off rather than to turn edit on.

commits.subject: A message said on a category's tab is kept in that category too

body.text: Every message spoken or copied is kept in Library as a phrase of its own; said on a category of the person's own, it now goes in that category as well, where Save would file it, so a sentence said on a tab is there on the tab afterwards. Said on Library or a record, it is in no category, as before; and words Library has already are not filed, since what typing finds comes from Library whichever tab is showing.

commits.subject: A guide section on a smaller keyboard on a phone or tablet

body.text: What iPhone, iPad, Gboard and Samsung Keyboard each offer to make the onscreen keyboard take less of the screen — one-handed and floating modes, the keyboard height, the row of suggestions turned off — beside the keyboard coming up only when the message box is tapped, and Peri's own as the alternative.

commits.subject: A head mouse held still on a magnified phrase chooses it, on an iPad

body.text: On an iPad driven by a head mouse, resting on a phrase magnified it and then did nothing: no words in the box, nothing said. The magnified cell grew in from 85%, smaller than its place for its first frames, so a pointer near its edge was briefly off it — and iPadOS said the still pointer had left and come back, which the guard against a control arriving under a still pointer refused until the pointer moved, as a still head never does.

The cell now fades in at its full size, covering its place from the first frame; and a control the pointer is said to leave and come back to without moving carries on as the pointer that never left. One refused when it came stays refused.

commits.subject: The phone's keyboard only when asked for: a tap, a click or a dwell in a box

body.text: On a phone, Peri's habit of keeping the caret in the message box raised the system keyboard after every tap on the board, over half the screen.

The message and question boxes now want no system keyboard (inputMode none) until a click, a tap or a dwell in one asks for it, and a press or a dwell anywhere else puts it away; they keep their caret all the same, so a hardware keyboard and Peri's own still type into them. After a finger, with Peri's own keyboard off, Peri also stops putting the caret back on its own, and a finger's press lets focus go. While resting, no system keyboard at all: the caret comes out of the box, nothing puts it back, and a tap cannot raise one.

commits.subject: A phone's tab row keeps room enough for the runner's wider font

body.text: Customize is always on a phone's row now, which left three tabs, the plus and the order button fitting with five pixels to spare on a Mac and not at all in the CI runner's wider Linux font. The glyphs and the tabs give back a little padding, which leaves thirty.

commits.subject: Debounced arrows; Customize gold while tabs have no room; a phone's tab showing keeps to its name

body.text: The arrows over the grid page no more than once every half second, and not while the grid is still moving from the last page, so a rest and a gaze rig's click after it page once.

Customize is the brand's gold while tabs on the bar have no room on its row — the colour its tiles say No room in. On a narrow screen the tab showing keeps to its name, with no eye or drag pad, and Customize is always on the row, where hiding and moving are done instead. Phone tabs take a little less padding, which the runner's wider Linux font needed for three tabs and the plus to fit beside the order button.

commits.subject: Tabs in every mode, hideable behind Customize; the tab and table one surface; two arrows over the grid

body.text: The category tabs work the same in auto-speak as in edit mode: the tab showing renames where it stands, carries its drag pad and its bin, and the plus adds a category, whichever mode is on.

Every tab can be hidden, by an eye on the tab showing — Library and Translations too — which goes on to the next tab still on the bar. More is a customize glyph now, there whenever a tab is off the bar for room or hidden: a grid of every tab where one is chosen, shown or hidden by its eye, and a category moved by its drag pad, nothing changing until Done. Tiles the bar has no room for say "No room", worked out again as the grid and the screen change. The hidden list is this device's view, kept under the account and in no backup or snapshot, and named in the privacy policy with the order each tab is shown in.
The tab showing and the phrase table blend into one surface: the tab stands over the table's edge where they meet, and its foot flares into the table as a Chrome tab's does.

The grid's scroll rail is two translucent arrows floating over its rightmost column, each half a cell high and a third of one wide, paging five sixths of the view and landing so the top row is whole. The phrase order control is at the right end of the tab row.

commits.subject: Release notes gather the versions under their major release

body.text: A level above the versions: each major release — Version 11 down to Version 1 — folds open onto its versions, with the days they span and how many releases it holds. The newest major and its newest version open on arrival; another major opens folded; one open at a time at every level.

commits.subject: Release notes in the menu, after Help: every version, each change folding open onto its commit

body.text: Menu → Release notes lists every version Peri has been, newest first, each dated and counted, the one running marked. A version folds open onto the changes it brought, and each change onto what its commit says, in paragraphs and lists: the guide's folds, one open at a time at each level.

The notes are the history rather than anything written by hand. `pnpm release` writes them into the version commit, from every commit since the version before, trailers taken off; everything before releases were numbered went out as 1.0.0. A test holds the file to package.json's version. They load only when the panel opens — 100KB compressed that the board never waits for.

commits.subject: The Keep it browser test reads the fill off the page, not through a locator that waits for it

body.text: Once Keep answered, the next look at its bar waited for an element that had gone with the question, until the test timed out — on the CI runner, where the question closed between the check and the look.

commits.subject: The open phrase carries its bin and drag pad; the bin's question holds everything; Enter and Escape in the box

body.text: Phrases and the emergency bar now work like the category tabs. In edit mode the phrase open in the box carries a bin against its cell's left edge and a drag pad against its right, each on the cell's ground two shades lighter; the emergency phrase open there does the same on its button. The rail's arrange toggle, the bar's reorder toggle and Delete in the card's row are gone. The open phrase stays on the board, first, once it is being changed and the tab or a search would leave it out.

The bin asks first, and the question holds everything until it is answered: neither answer arms until the pointer has gone 120px from the bin, both fill as they are rested on, every key but Enter (confirm) and Escape (keep) is swallowed, and it stands over the whole screen.

While the box holds a phrase as it was opened, nothing on the grid is chosen or magnified; the emergency bar stays live and, with anything in the box, speaks rather than inserting. Enter in the message box speaks, or saves in edit mode; Escape empties it; Enter with any modifier is a new line.

commits.subject: The clipboard keeps the top line's left end; paste goes to the field with the caret

items: On a narrow card the clipboard stays at the left end of the top line, the modes after it and the menu at its right end, the modes centred between the two and wrapping there on the narrowest phone; the language and the voice on the line under them. The groups are 0.75rem apart there, which keeps a 360px phone's modes on one line.

Paste goes into the field with the caret - the question, a link's text or address, a category's name - through the writer Peri's keyboard types with, and into the message as before where the message has it.

commits.subject: The edit prompt fits one line in Linux's wider font too

body.text: "Write or pick a phrase" measured 238px against 231px of room on the CI runner's font, which is wider than macOS's; "Write or choose one" leaves room in both, and shares its verb with "Choose a phrase".

commits.subject: One panel for the tab and the phrases; the box grounded; the menu and the question inside the card

body.text: The top row and the tabs: - The message and question cards have no ground, edge or shadow; the message box has the ground, and each box says focus with a line along its foot. - The top row and the tab bar have no ground, and no rule between them. - The tab showing and the phrase table are one panel - one ground, one edge, the tab covering the table's top edge - and the table's corners are rounded. The phrases are a step lighter, the page a step darker. Only the tab showing has a ground; the others' names are a step dimmer. - The drag pad shows only with five tabs or more on the bar. - Edit mode greens the panel's edge, muted, not the phrases; the box's dashed edge is dimmer. - The menu is in the card, last in its row of controls, well clear of the voice; on a narrow card at the right end of the modes' line. The busy indicator stands over the lower right of the phrase table.

The boxes: - The question's line is inside the message box, left of the message's on a wide screen and above it on a narrow one. The live microphone glyph is gone; the line along the foot of the question box pulses, slowly, while the microphone listens. - The prompts fit one line on a 320px phone: "Choose a phrase", "Write or pick a phrase", "Say or type a question".
The emergency bar: - Words the bar cuts off are shown whole and large in the middle of the phrase table while their button is rested on.

commits.subject: The tab showing carries its own tools; Rest is the row of controls, with Resume

body.text: Category tabs, in edit mode: - The tab showing carries a drag pad flush with its right edge. A rest on its name makes it a field where it stands; while renaming, a bin that asks first is the only control on it. Enter, another tab, leaving edit mode or the field losing the caret save the name; Escape puts it back. - The drag pad lifts the tab, blue; a dwell on another tab drops it there, and the pad again puts it back. A mouse can drag any category. - A tab showing that More would hide is drawn as itself before More. - Adding a category is a plus right after the last tab, as a browser's new tab button is. The pencil, reorder and A-Z tools at the bar's end are gone. - The category dialog is adding one and asking before a delete.

Rest: - Only the open space in the message card's row of controls rests the app. - While resting, Resume covers that row - muted brand gold, near-black text - and Paused stands large in the middle of the screen. - After Rest or Resume, neither answers until the pointer has left the row.

commits.subject: Browser tests keep the pointer off the top row's open space

body.text: Rest is the top row's open space now, and the pointer starts at the page's corner, which is in it: on CI a test that left it there rested the app and could not click the edit toggle. The harness moves the pointer off the page once the board is open. The Speak test rests its pointer on what is open space on the wide screen before the screen narrows; it gets a two-second action dwell, still under the three seconds each of its waits gives Speak.

commits.subject: Rest is the top row's open space

body.text: The Rest bar is gone. A surface behind everything in the top row takes the pointer wherever nothing in the row answers - the cards, the rows in them and the padding round them pass it through, and the controls and the boxes keep it - so a dwell or a click on any open space switches dwelling off, and the same again switches it back on. A rest fills along the foot of the row; while resting, the open space is washed in the rest colour under a row dimmed because none of it will answer.

commits.subject: Tabs with More, a magnified cell, the new order after speaking, and saving into the tab showing

items: The category bar has no arrows: tabs drawn as tabs, one row of them, and More for the rest, a grid of every category that names the one showing while it hides it. A tab's name is cut to seven characters unless it is the tab showing. How many fit is worked out from measured widths in core/tab-rows.ts.

A phrase cell holds one line of words to 15rem, cut with an ellipsis; the cell under the pointer is magnified over its neighbours, its words in lines up to 30rem, moving nothing else and put back whenever the board moves.
The board takes its new order whenever something said comes to an end, and where that moved a cell nothing can be chosen until the pointer has moved 20px.

Edit mode chooses no category: Save files a phrase under the tab showing, or Library alone, and never makes a second copy - words already on the board put that phrase in the category showing instead. Nothing beside the words says what is being edited; words already on the board are said in a toast.

commits.subject: Link fields follow the box: gone with the link, a new link shown as itself, and editing one is not typing

Speak in edit mode: test the phrase's own voice; let Save refuse what it refuses
Two ways of working: edit mode builds a sentence at the caret, and Speak there saves

body.text: Compose mode is gone. Turning auto-speak off turns edit mode on, and the other way round. In edit mode a phrase chosen into an empty box opens; into words it goes in at the caret, a blank selected. Speak sits after Save and says the phrase being written as it saves it. Auto-speak keeps what it says as written, so a phrase ending in a full stop is no longer kept a second time without one.

Auto-speak puts the phrase it said in the message box, selected

Synchronize the presentation background: named in the board, carried as a clip

Test presentation mode: the stage, the toggle, the window, the camera and the picture

Read the toast's ring in the format Chrome reports a mixed colour

Say what the toast looks like, and why

A preview branch that development lands on; main is production, moved by pnpm promote

items: preview is the default branch: every pull request is based on it and merges into it, under the ruleset main had. main keeps that ruleset with one way past it, a repository admin.

pnpm promote (tools/promote.ts) refuses a preview that does not end in a release or whose check or browser did not pass, fast-forwards main to it with the signed-in admin's own rights, and runs the Publish workflow. No new secret; every workflow token stays read-only.
CI runs on pushes to preview as well as main; pnpm release refuses to run on either. README, CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS.md describe the two branches.

commits.subject: Start a new phrase with the same X as Clear

body.text: In edit mode the slot at the left end of the line starts a new phrase, which empties the box as Clear does, so it now draws the same heavy muted-red X rather than a plus. The guide names it as Clear.

commits.subject: Centre Clear, Undo and New on the words, however many lines they run to

body.text: The slot that empties the box stood level with the last line of text. It is now centred on the box, which pads its words equally above and below, so on the words themselves — in the message card and the question's.

commits.subject: Place Save and Speak again as soon as the box has settled after a mode switch

body.text: A trace from a real screen showed that after switching modes the topbar's fit laid the hidden copy out at the box's new width, while Save stayed where the other mode had it until something else redrew the bar, about seven seconds later or when the pointer moved. The fit now tells AfterText to place its control again (PLACE_AGAIN, dispatched on the copy), and AfterText also watches the copy's size.

commits.subject: Hold the dwells when a mode switch moves the box under the pointer; place Save and Speak on every render

items: A mode switch can rearrange the message card under the pointer that made it: leaving edit mode shrank the row of controls and the message box slid up under the resting pointer, whose caret dwell put the caret at the start of the words, so what was typed next went in front. The switch now notes what a rest would reach and, once laid out, holds the dwells until the pointer moves if that changed (holdIfMovedUnder). Nothing moved, nothing held.

AfterText places its control again on every render and in the frame after, rather than only when a resize is reported, so a mode switch that rewraps the words without changing them cannot leave Save or Speak where the other mode had it. The box is re-fitted on a mode change too.

commits.subject: Lay out the copy that places Save and Speak at the box's exact width

body.text: AfterText finds where the words end by laying them out in a hidden copy of the box, and the copy was given offsetWidth, which rounds. A box flex shares a line out to is fractional (387.11px), so wherever a line's last word fitted only in that fraction the copy broke the line a word early and Save or Speak stood after the wrong word. A mode switch changes what the box shares its line with, which is where it showed. Both places that size the copy now use getBoundingClientRect().width.

commits.subject: Save after the last word when edit mode rewraps the words

body.text: Edit mode puts what is being edited at the right end of the line, narrowing the box under words that do not change. The box re-fitted its height only when its text changed or the window resized, so the rewrapped words outgrew it and Save, kept inside it, was drawn on the wrong line. The box now re-fits when its own width changes.

commits.subject: What is being edited at the right end of the line the words are written on

body.text: The "Editing phrase" title and the category trigger move from a row under the line to its right end, 0.75rem clear of the words. A narrow card gives them a line of their own under the words, still at the right.

commits.subject: Focus always in a box, the question's while it is open; the menu a bare glyph

items: Focus goes to the question box as it opens and back to the message box as it closes, and is put back whenever it falls to nothing, with the message box's own caret. Focus moved elsewhere by Tab or into another field is left.
The menu button has no ground or edge of its own.

commits.subject: No button takes focus; switching modes changes nothing in the box or the grid

items: A press on any dwell control leaves focus, and the caret, where it was, so the next key typed goes into the message. Tab still reaches every control; something being dragged is left to the browser.

Leaving edit mode, what the box holds becomes the message: the words, the caret and the word being typed, so the grid stays narrowed to it. A phrase with choices is carried as the board shows it. Between auto-speak and building a message nothing moves. The microphone does not carry the draft, since it empties the box anyway.

commits.subject: Typing searches the board in edit mode, as it does everywhere else

body.text: One rule for what has been typed (talk/typed.ts), shared by the message and the phrase being edited: what was put in the box is finished and narrows nothing, and what is typed after it searches Library, up to the caret. Opening a phrase off a narrowed grid lets the whole tab back and holds the dwells; turning edit mode on still changes nothing in the grid.

commits.subject: Edit mode changes nothing on screen; a question starts with an empty box, edit mode and please off

items: Turning edit mode on keeps the message box's words and the grid as they were: the tab, the scroll position, and the word it was narrowed to, which is held until the box is emptied. It no longer goes to Library, marks the phrase or scrolls to it. Arranging by hand waits while the grid is narrowed.
Opening the question empties the message box (Undo brings it back), and turns off edit mode and please.

commits.subject: Please, the built-in tabs first, the bin only when there is something to delete, and a red X for Clear

items: A please toggle after auto-speak: ", please" on the end of everything said, in the language it is said in, and never in the phrase, what is kept, what is copied or the Translations record. Never waited for on the emergency bar.
The tabs always begin Translations, Answers (when there are some), Library, then the categories in the order chosen.
Delete in edit mode is unseen until there is something to delete, its place kept so nothing beside it moves.
Clear is a heavy X in a muted red.
On a narrow card the language and voice wrap rather than push the row past the card's edge.

commits.subject: Speak a rem further from the words, the menu in the upper right, Ask filled as Speak is, and quieter language, voice and tab

items: Speak, Save and Ask stand a rem and a few pixels after the last word; on a line of their own they start level with the words.
The menu is in the upper right corner; the keyboard stays at the left. The busy indicator moves left of the menu rather than over it.
The language and the voice have no ground of their own.
Ask is filled in the accent, as Speak is, and grey when it cannot be used.
The tab that is showing is a faint green ground and a green edge rather than filled; choosing one still flashes full.

commits.subject: The controls row on top, and Speak right after the last word typed

body.text: The card's row of controls — clipboard, centred modes, values — moves above the line the words are written on. Speak (Save in edit mode) stands right after the last word, and Ask after the question's: ui/after-text.tsx lays out a never-seen copy of the box with a space the control's width at the end of the words, and puts the control where that space lands — after the last word, or at the start of the next line, the box growing to hold it.

It moves with every letter, so holdIfUnderPointer holds the dwells when it lands under a resting pointer or goes from under one (Save vanishing left the caret dwell under the pointer, which wiped the new phrase's mark and its toast); placed again where it stood, it has not arrived. The box's height is measured from the copy at the box's new width on a resize.

commits.subject: Clear at the left end of the input line, Speak at its right once there are words; copy and paste far left, the modes centred

body.text: The message card's line: Clear (Undo, or start a new phrase) at its left end, the box, and Speak (Save in edit mode) at its right end — drawn only once there are words, in a place kept for it so the box never changes width. The question card's line the same: Clear/Undo left, Ask right once there is a question. Under the line, a three-column row: copy and paste at the far left, the microphone and the modes centred, the language, the voice and, in edit mode, Delete at the right. A narrow card stacks the row, asked of the card's own width.

commits.subject: The message and question boxes as cards, with their controls in a row inside

body.text: Shaped like a chat app's input box: the words, and inside the card along the bottom one row — the microphone and the three modes at its start; clear, copy, paste, the language and the voice, and Speak filled in the accent at its end. A narrow card wraps the end group onto its own line. What is being edited is a row of its own below the controls, so edit mode moves nothing in the row. The question is a card too, dashed. Opening or closing it holds the dwells, since the message card moves.

Replaces the controls riding the boxes' borders. The gaps are 1.25rem across and 0.75rem between wrapped lines, so no two controls' invisible areas overlap; the browser tests measure it at 360, 390 and 1280px in both modes.

commits.subject: Copy and paste to the right of clear and undo, on the message box's lower border

body.text: The upper right is what becomes of the message: speak, or in edit mode delete and save. Copy and paste work on the text where it stands, with the slot that empties the box. Paste is there in both modes; copy only outside edit mode, as before.

commits.subject: Revert #142, #143 and #144: the speaking tab, and the corrected claims

body.text: Takes away the speaking tab (#142) and its move into the menu (#144), and the correction of two claims (#143): that the emergency bar always uses the device voice, and that the app has no access to the microphone. The tree is 7.5.11's again, but for the version.

commits.subject: Hold the guide's Overview to every item in the menu
The speaking tab opens from the menu, not Settings

body.text: It is a place somebody goes rather than a value they set, like the guide or Backup & sharing. A click opens it and closes the menu; a refused rest leaves the menu open and says so under the item, with the address. Its own icon, in the guide's table, shown in the Overview's menu line.

commits.subject: Say what the emergency bar and the microphone actually do

body.text: The emergency bar plays an ElevenLabs clip already loaded and the device voice otherwise; it was said to always use the device voice, in the guide, the ElevenLabs row and the privacy policy. And the privacy policy said the app has no access to the microphone, which listen mode uses. A test holds all three to neither claim.

commits.subject: The speaking tab: the last thing said, shown and played in a tab of its own, for sharing into a call instead of the board

body.text: A call sends the microphone and cancels the speakers out of it, so nobody on the other end heard Peri. A shared tab's own sound goes to the call as a stream of its own, so the speaking tab plays the ElevenLabs clip itself and Peri stays quiet while it is open. A device voice is played by the operating system, not the tab — measured in Chrome — so the tab shows its words.
Opened from Settings by a click; a handed clip is answered, and played here on a refusal or after ANSWER_MS of nothing, so nothing goes unsaid.

commits.subject: The map: every icon in ui/icons.tsx, and why
Hold the icon table itself, not the file around it, to every icon
Every icon the app draws in ui/icons.tsx and in the guide's table; the guide shows them
Resting, auto-speak and the emergency bar straight after the overview
Formatting and auto-speak straight after the overview; the overview opens in auto-speak
Hold the toast to the middle of the table's upper third
Toast in the upper third of the phrase table, ring 1.3rem
Name each icon the first time a section of the guide uses it
Update undici, nanoid and brace-expansion past their advisories

body.text: All three are development tools — jsdom's HTTP client, PostCSS's id generator under Vite, and ESLint's glob expansion — so nothing shipped changes: the production build is byte-for-byte the one before.

commits.subject: The guide's section count, and its test in the map
Bring the guide up to date with the app, and the sign-in page's promise with it
Toast on a lighter ground, ringed in it at 85%
Toast ring in the phrase cell's colour at 80%, words in a muted accent
Toast ring from #111 to #888 at 60%, corners 0.8rem
A roomier toast, ringed with a 2rem gradient at 40%, as wide as a phone allows
Getting started beside the board on a wide screen
Test the board deaf for a moment after Getting started closes
Getting started: the guide a part at a time, opening on signing in
Done on the category grid keeps a translation or an answer as a phrase
Browser tests: Done on where a new phrase goes saves it
Done on the category grid saves a phrase being written
Test a translation left unfiled and the next phrase starting where the last went
Done on the category grid files a phrase on the board without the check
Keep a Sent list from before until Library holding it is kept
Test a list with nothing new going, and a filled-in phrase kept in auto-speak
Keep what is said in Library; no Sent tab

body.text: Every message spoken or copied is kept in Library as a phrase in no category, unless Library says it already, and counted as used the moment it is — so it is first among what typing finds and first under Recently used. The Sent tab is gone; a board's Sent list is brought into Library once as it opens, and the key taken away. The privacy policy, the guide and the suggested-answers row say that a kept message is a phrase, and goes wherever phrases go.

commits.subject: A hyphen splits words for the initials too
Only what a test can tell apart in the punctuation a word starts past
A hyphen splits words for search, as a space does
Search inside a phrase only where a word begins

body.text: Typing matched any stretch of a phrase, so a few letters pulled in every phrase with them mid-word: "at" found that, what and water. The second group now holds phrases with a word beginning with what was typed, a word beginning at its first character and again past a quote or bracket.

commits.subject: Test keeping a category's place, ticking two, and a sheet taking a reference away
App tests, browser tests and docs for categories as references
Core tests for Library and references
Library holds every phrase; categories hold ordered references to them (tests to follow)
Test what an edit inside a phrase, a clear and an answer do to the search
Search Library for what is typed, in three groups each by recency
Say when a category goes by itself
Drop a category with its last phrase, and every empty one after an import
Take out Jamaican Patois and Puerto Rican Spanish
Say that punctuation-only copies went, and which stayed
Fold each unpunctuated near-duplicate into its punctuated twin
Say what Library is, in the guide, AGENTS.md and the decisions
Move the browser tests onto Library and categories of their own
Collapse every shipped category into Library, and each wording into one phrase
Document deleting a category, and hold its layout in the browser
Test the draft filed by hand under a deleted category
Delete a category from its rename dialog, asking first
Move the decisions out of AGENTS.md into docs/decisions

body.text: AGENTS.md was 248 KB, loaded into every agent session before any work began, and growing by a paragraph a pull request. It keeps the map, the testing and styling rules, versioning and the release process — and now a short list of the rules that reach across the whole app, each linked to where it is argued — at 89 KB.

The twenty-two sections on why each part is the shape it is moved into docs/decisions/, one file a topic, whole: nothing was rewritten. Every cross-reference between them became a link, and structure.test.ts now holds every link, file and anchor to landing, and every backticked name in the decisions to existing, as it already did for AGENTS.md.

commits.subject: Split the stylesheet into parts, in the order it was written

body.text: src/index.css was 4,461 lines, ordered by when a rule was written rather than by what it styles, and AGENTS.md warned against splitting it because moving a rule past another changes the cascade and jsdom would not notice.

So nothing moved. src/styles/ holds thirteen contiguous runs of it, cut where a section began, imported by index.css in their places — and the production CSS is byte for byte what it was, down to the hash in its filename. Each part says what is in it, including what accreted.
Tests read the stylesheet through tests/stylesheet.ts, which inlines the parts in order, and structure.test.ts holds every part to being imported exactly once.

commits.subject: Split the store into parts behind the same barrel

body.text: core/store.ts was 1,751 lines: settings, the phrase store, the word lists, every record of what was said, the accounts, the day's conversation, whose board it is, and the reset. It is twelve modules under core/store/ now, one for each kind of thing kept, and store.ts re-exports exactly the 101 names it always offered, so nothing that imports it changed.

The parts import each other directly, never through the barrel, so no cycle runs through it. The one knot — the sign-in handoff reads settings while settings are read through the owner — is untied by the handoff living in settings.ts. The reset's list of keys moved back beside the keys, which is what the comment on it says is the point.

commits.subject: Move three concerns out of talk.tsx into hooks of their own

body.text: talk.tsx had grown to 1,346 lines, with every feature landing there. The concerns with a narrow way in and out now live beside it, in the use-board / use-composer / use-editor pattern: synchronizing (use-synchronized.ts), the strip that says storage has stopped keeping changes (use-not-keeping.ts), and the grid's order and what it shows (use-grid-order.ts). Code and comments moved verbatim; no behaviour changes. talk.tsx is 1,109 lines.
setMode stays: it reaches a dozen things across the screen, and a hook taking all of them as arguments would move the file without dividing it.

commits.subject: Run the browser tests in CI

body.text: jsdom lays nothing out, and AGENTS.md said so in seven places rather than testing any of it. The checks I made by hand against a preview for every recent change were thrown away after each one.

They are tests/e2e/ now, run by Playwright against the production build in Chromium: where a new phrase goes and whether the board shows it, a sentence built from two categories, the board carrying on over refused storage and a damaged store, and the layout rules jsdom cannot see — the portrait phone, the short screen, no sideways scroll, the box that grows, the mode strip on its border. Each was shown to fail with the fix it guards taken out, and 45 of 45 passed over three repeats.
A browser job in CI runs them beside check, uploading traces when red. Not required by the ruleset yet.

commits.subject: Fix the agents guide's stale names, and hold it to the project

body.text: AGENTS.md named tests/app/App.test.tsx in six places after it was split into nine files, three paths from before the source was layered, and two names renamed the day after they were written down — FilterBar's centreOn and talk.tsx's landed, both now pointing — plus orderEmergency, long since orderByIds. An agent following the map was sent looking for things that are not there.

structure.test.ts now checks every backticked path and identifier in it against the project, the way it already checked the README's commands and links. A name kept only as history goes without backticks.

commits.subject: Pin the pencil quiet while reordering, on a real category
Let tabs move between categories in edit mode; rename with a pencil

body.text: A tab opened its category for renaming in edit mode, which left edit mode unable to move between categories at all: editing a phrase under another tab meant leaving the mode, going there and coming back. A tab now goes to its category in every mode, and renaming is a pencil among the bar's own tools, acting on the tab that is showing — quiet on a tab that is not a category and while the tabs are being arranged.
A blank draft follows the tab it arrives at in edit mode; one with words or a picked category stays where it is.

That exposed the category grid writing each tile into the draft as it was rested on and putting the first back on Cancel, which marked a draft as started just for being looked at. It now holds the choice until Done, as the other grids do.

commits.subject: Insert at the composer's caret, not the box's

body.text: A box without focus does not keep its caret. Chrome puts it back to the start when a category tab is rested on — no event, no call on the box — and the next phrase chosen went in before the one before it. It was unreachable while choosing a phrase took the tabs away, and turned up in a browser the moment that stopped.
insert now reads cursorPos, which is where the word the board narrows to was already read from, so the two agree on where the caret is.

commits.subject: Remember where a phrase ended through Undo, and pin the rest
Keep a phrase whole when another is chosen after it

body.text: Choosing a phrase left the caret against its last word, and the board read that as a word being typed. It narrowed the grid to it and took the category bar away, and the next phrase chosen replaced that word as if finishing it: "Once in a blue moon" and then "Moonlight becomes you" came out as "Once in a blue Moonlight becomes you". A sentence from two categories could not be built without typing a space first.

The composer now knows where a phrase it put in ends, while nothing has been typed since, and there is no word being typed at that point: the board stays whole, the tabs stay, and the next phrase goes after it. Anything the person writes clears it, so a typed word still narrows and is still finished by the next phrase.
Three sorting tests had written the overwrite in as expected while testing the gaze guard; they now expect both phrases whole.

commits.subject: Keep a toast up until the next dwell

body.text: It went after two seconds, and for a save, a refused paste or a link the browser would not open it is the only thing that says anything at all — a gaze on the board rather than on the corner could miss the whole of it. It now stays until the next dwell, the rule the mark on the last phrase said follows, with a ten-second ceiling for a board nobody is working.

commits.subject: Put a deleted phrase back

body.text: Deleting was the one change the app offered no way back from, and the bin sits a dwell's breadth from Save. The slot at the box's lower left, which starts a new phrase and has nothing to do the moment after a delete, now offers the phrase back by name.

removePhrase hands back what it took — the entry, or the fact of hiding it, and its places on the emergency bar and in its category's arrangement — and forgetUsed hands back the count. Undo puts all of it back where it was and opens the phrase in the box, where it was when the bin took it. Anything written or opened afterwards takes the offer away.

commits.subject: Drop a damaged phrase rather than the whole board

body.text: loadPhraseStore checked that the phrases somebody wrote were a list and nothing about what was in it, and the same for the overrides, hidden ids, renames and moves. A phrase whose words were not words reached the parser while the board was drawn and threw — on every load, since the damage stays in storage. Found in a browser while checking the crash screen: Start again would only have started the crash again.
Each list and record now keeps the entries of the right shape and drops the rest.

commits.subject: Hold the dwells as the strip arrives, and pin it
Keep the emergency bar up when the app fails, and never let a write crash it

body.text: Every write to storage was bare, several of them inside React state updates, and there was no error boundary anywhere. A refused write — a full store, a private window — threw out of the update and unmounted the whole tree: a blank page, the emergency bar with it, on a device somebody may have no other way to speak with.

Every write now goes through writeKey, which reports which record and never what was in it, tells its listeners, and returns false. The board carries on from memory, and a strip at the top says that changes are no longer being kept, with a backup built from memory — the one place the unsaved changes are.

A render that throws now puts up the emergency bar as this person arranged it, read afresh from storage, with Start again and a backup. The derivations it needs moved out of the use-board hook into core/board.ts, so the bar cannot come out differently there.

commits.subject: Say what the successor map guards, and no more
Move suggested replies to Opus 5.5, and give thinking models room

body.text: Opus 5 went to legacy on 22 September. Two things had to come with the new id rather than after it.

A model the list stops offering fell back to the default, which is the quickest — so the swap alone would have moved everybody who chose Opus down to Haiku, from their settings, backups and synced boards alike. The old id is now read as its successor.

Opus 5.5 thinks before every answer and cannot be asked not to, and the thinking is paid out of the same max_tokens as the answers. At 1,200 it could spend the lot before writing a line. Fable 5.1 was already in that position. Both now get room for both and are asked for low effort; Haiku, which refuses an effort at all, is sent none.

commits.subject: Write down opening on the phrase itself
Pin what the toast says it opened
Open the editor on the phrase, not on a copy of it

body.text: The board had just gone and found the phrase, marked its cell and brought it into view — and then handed over a copy of it that could not be saved. What that cost was a dwell spent finding again the cell the board had just finished pointing at.
The box holds the phrase as it was written, source and all, its own category and voice are what the strip shows, and Save saves it.

commits.subject: Write down going to the phrase the message is
Pin the board to staying awake where it did not move
Go to the phrase the message already is

body.text: A message box holding one phrase — which is what it holds the moment one is chosen while composing — is somebody pointing at that phrase. What they got for reaching for edit mode was a copy of it, filed wherever they happened to be standing, that could not be saved and said only "Already on the board".

Now the board goes and finds it: its category, the cell marked and brought into view, the tab brought to the middle of the bar. Off All too, unlike a phrase just saved, because the question here is which category the phrase is in and All is the one tab that cannot answer it.
What the grid and the bar watch is an occasion rather than a phrase's name, so the same phrase composed twice is answered twice.

commits.subject: Write down what the board does to show where a phrase went
Ask for the cell once, on the phrase
Show them where the new phrase went

body.text: A save left one more cell among a couple of thousand and a line of text that fades. Three things answer that now: the cell takes the mark the last phrase chosen takes, the grid brings it into view, and the bar brings the tab to its middle where the board moved by itself.

The window is grown to reach it. It starts again at a screenful on arriving at a tab and a category runs to a hundred and eighty phrases, so the new cell is often past the end of what is rendered — and a cell that does not exist is nothing to scroll to.

commits.subject: Write down what a new phrase does to the board
Pin the emergency bar, the hold and the tab that did not move
Follow a new phrase to the category it was filed under

body.text: Filed anywhere but the tab in front of them, a phrase lands among a couple of thousand cells, and all somebody has to show for writing one is a line of text that fades.

Three cases do not move, and none of them is an exception to that: on All the phrase is already there, the emergency bar is on screen under every tab, and a phrase being reworded is one somebody is moving out of where they are — refiling several out of one category is a run they would be thrown out of after the first.

commits.subject: Hold the filing to the way in, the voice beside it and a reload
File a new phrase under the tab in front of them

body.text: Somebody who switches to a category and then reaches for edit mode is adding to that category, nearly every time. What they got instead was a picker landing on wherever the last phrase went — which after one trip to another tab is the wrong answer for every phrase after it, each costing three dwells to put right.

Only where the tab is a category. All is every category at once, and Sent, Answers and Translations are records of what was said, so none of the four is somewhere a phrase can be filed: those leave the last choice standing rather than throwing it away and making somebody pick again.
Only on the way in, too. A draft that refiled itself whenever somebody glanced at another tab would move a phrase they had already chosen a category for.

commits.subject: Hold the question box to two tools, and the keyboard to the setting that offered it
Take the translate control off the question box, and offer the keyboard only where it is wanted

body.text: Two things somebody using this board did not ask for, both taken out of the way.

The question box no longer reads a heard question in the board's own language. A translation of somebody else's words is not what that box is for — it holds what was said so it can be answered — and the model reads a question in the language it was asked in just as well. The control, the line it drew under the box, translateHeard and the tests and disclosures behind it are all gone.

Peri's own keyboard is now a setting, off until it is asked for. It is the only way to type at all on iOS, where a dwell raises no system keyboard, and a target in the way on a device with a real one. It does not travel between devices, for the reason the text size does not: which keyboard a device can raise is about the device in front of somebody.

commits.subject: Ask the apology tests about the hour and the abandoned question
Say something while a reply is being written

body.text: Three seconds is a long silence with somebody standing in front of you. A reply can take several, and the person using the board cannot fill that — filling it is what they came here for. So the board fills it for them: one short apology, said aloud, once a question.

It is the board's sentence and not theirs. It is said through speak and recorded nowhere: not in the Sent list, not counted towards any phrase, not in the conversation the next reply is written against. It is said instantly, for the reason the emergency bar is, since this fills a wait and cannot start one of its own.

Never the same words twice within the hour, because a machine that says the same sentence every time is a machine somebody is listening to rather than a person they are talking to. Five are kept ready — the failure this covers is a wait, so it cannot be fetched during one — topped up after one is said and at no other time, with a shipped set behind them for a board with no key, no network, or nothing written yet.
The request that fills them carries nothing of anybody's: no question, no phrase off the board, no conversation. The Settings row, the guide and the privacy policy all say so.

commits.subject: Hold the Sent tab's order while somebody is looking at it

body.text: Saying a message again moves it to the front of the record, so on the tab it was said from the cell just used slid out from under the gaze that used it — the same thing an order that goes by use did to the board, fixed the same way.

heldOrder keeps the order the tab was opened in, with anything said since at the front: this list is newest first, so something arriving is new rather than moved, and it is what somebody is most likely to be looking for.

commits.subject: Ask the order tests about an order that reads the record
Rearrange the board when the tab changes, not when a phrase is chosen

body.text: An order that goes by use was applied on the very dwell that chose a phrase: the cell just used slid to the front, everything else moved around it, and the next thing somebody went looking for was not where they had left it. On a board read by gaze that is the worst moment to move anything.

The counting still happens on that dwell. What the board is ordered by is a copy of the record, taken when somebody changes what they are looking at — another tab, or another order — so a board being read holds still and a tab arrived at is already in the order those counts make.

What still moves the board as a phrase is chosen is composing, which narrows the grid to the word at the caret. That is what the dwell guard is for now, and it is asked for only there: auto-speak moves nothing.

commits.subject: Bring CONTRIBUTING up to what the project is now

body.text: It had a five-thousand-line file's worth of drift in it: App.tsx called fifty lines when it is a hundred and thirty, and a layering of four directories when there are seven layers.

What it was missing is the set of properties a change can break without anything looking broken — the emergency bar never waiting on a network, a suggested answer never being spoken by itself, a phrase never failing into silence, a disclosure being written in the three places that have to agree, a board belonging to the account signed in, and no client secret anywhere. Each is argued out in AGENTS.md; what belongs here is that they are not anybody's to trade away in passing.

Also: what to do about two targets in one place, that a test which clicks proves nothing about a rest, and that a file added to public/ is asked for over the network rather than served from the worker's cache.

commits.subject: Write a README, and hold it to what the project has

body.text: What Peri is, and the thing nothing wrote down: which of GitHub and Netlify decides what. Both run on every push and both report a check, so the division is worth stating — Actions decides whether a change may merge, Netlify builds and serves, and publishing is a separate decision.

It also has the table of where every secret lives: the one Actions secret, the VITE_* variables that are public by the time they reach a browser, the unrestricted key that never leaves a command line, and the three that belong to the user and never leave their device.

A test holds both this and CONTRIBUTING.md to naming no command the project does not have and no file that is not there. CONTRIBUTING kept several claims this year's changes had made false — that Netlify runs the tests, that the tree is not formatter-clean, that the grid renders every cell, and three paths that had moved.

commits.subject: Say what the grid renders, and what the app tests are now
Hold the tests' own grid viewport to windowing the board
Render a screenful before measuring, and split the app tests by subject

body.text: The grid rendered every cell in the table on its first pass and windowed down from what that measured, so opening the board mounted two and a half thousand cells — and so did every test that drives the app, which was most of the suite's running time. It starts from a screenful now, and still renders everything where nothing can be measured at all.

The tests get the grid's viewport from the setup, so they window as a browser does; the handful that are about the whole board ask for it. And App.test.tsx, five thousand lines and forty-six subjects, is nine files named after what they cover, over a shared harness.
The suite went from 210 seconds to 24.

commits.subject: Time a test out when it has hung, not when it is slow

body.text: The whole-app tests render every cell on the board, jsdom having no layout to window by, so one that loads the board a few times takes a second or two alone. Under the whole suite in parallel on a CI runner with fewer and slower cores, several passed Vitest's five seconds and the run went red on work that was fine.

commits.subject: Keep the version commit on the branch, where nothing needs to bypass main

body.text: A workflow committing the version to main would have to be allowed past main's own ruleset, and a repository can only grant that to a personal access token with write access to main kept in its secrets. `pnpm release` reads the pull request's label and writes the commit on the branch instead, which needs nothing of the sort.

commits.subject: Check on GitHub, release on main, publish on purpose

body.text: Netlify ran the suite as its build command, which was the only gate on anything merging. It made every deploy preview eight to ten minutes long, and each merge ran the suite twice: once for the change, and again for the commit that bumped the version.

items: GitHub Actions runs pnpm check on every pull request and on main, and a second check requires exactly one of the labels major, minor or patch. A ruleset on main requires both, and a pull request. Netlify now only builds, so previews are quick.

The version is bumped on main after the merge passes, by tools/release.ts, covering everything since the last release and taking the highest label among the pull requests it covers. It stands down when main has moved on, so nothing is versioned untested.

Publishing is its own workflow: it refuses anything but a released main, publishes Netlify's build of that commit, and then asks the site what it is serving. Auto-publishing stays off, because a release should reach people when somebody decides it should.

commits.subject: Ask the network first for anything whose address outlives a release

body.text: The service worker served every same-origin file from its cache first, including the manifest and the icons, which keep one address from release to release. So an installed copy went on calling itself by the app's old name: Chrome's check for a new manifest was answered with the one stored the day the worker installed, and nothing short of a new worker would ever have replaced it.

Cache first is now only for Vite's output under /assets/, whose names carry a hash of their contents. Everything else is asked for fresh and answered from the cache when there is no network. The cache is a new generation, so every installed copy picks up the worker and loses the cache holding the old manifest.
The worker's tests now run it, against a fake network and cache, rather than reading its text.

commits.subject: Keep each account's board to that account

body.text: Every storage key was global, so whoever signed in next on a device opened the last person's phrases, lists, settings, keys, Sent list and sync passphrase. Every read and write now names whose board it is.

items: The first account to open a board on a device keeps the names the board already had, so the board from before goes to whoever was using it without anything being moved. Every later owner's keys carry @owner, and every guest on a device shares one guest board.
Signed out is nobody's board. Signing out leaves the sign-in page the dwell times and text size of the board left, and a board opened for the first time starts from them.
Signing out reloads the page, so nothing held in memory or still in flight reaches whoever signs in next. A sign-in or sign-out in another tab reloads this one.
Remembered translations and stored audio follow the board, so a factory reset takes one board's and nobody else's.
The name Apple sends only once is kept per Apple account.

body.text: The guide, the privacy policy (with its own date now) and the sign-out dialog say what is kept for whom, and that this separates boards in the app rather than encrypting them on the device.

commits.subject: Make room for each box's own border when it grows

body.text: The height is border-box and scrollHeight leaves the border out, so a box set to exactly what its text measured was two pixels short of holding it. That was enough for the scroll arrows to appear on every box past one line, and the room they take rewrapped the text into a box that really did overflow — which is how the key message came to be cut off in a box with room to spare.
A grid test deleted jsdom's own offsetHeight after faking it, leaving every later test with none at all; it is put back now instead.

commits.subject: Take no question without a working key, and show the microphone only while it hears

body.text: The question box is for getting answers, and the answers are the user's own Anthropic account. With no key, or one Anthropic turned away, it now says so in the box — as its words, read-only, so the box grows to hold them — and listens to nobody. A key is checked with Anthropic before it is saved, by listing its models, which costs nothing.

The live microphone shows from the recogniser's audiostart to its audioend, rather than from the moment listening was asked for, which was while a permission prompt could still be up. It no longer pulses: the ground dimmed with the pulse and showed the border through it, and the glow lay on the border, so the border itself seemed to pulse. Only a level inside the capsule moves now, on a solid ground with no glow.
Typing in the box stops the microphone, and nothing it had heard is answered on its way out.

commits.subject: Pulse a microphone in the question box while it is listening

body.text: The box being open is not the microphone being on: the recogniser stops by itself when somebody stops talking, and clearing the box starts it again. A microphone at the right end of the box's lower border says which, drawn while it listens and at no other time — on the tools' ground and at their size, lit in the accent with a glow, and pulsing in brightness and glow as the resting lozenge does, so it says live from across a room. Nothing in the pulse moves, and under reduced motion it stays lit and still. Not a target. The guide and the privacy policy show the same glyph.

commits.subject: Show Peri's version, centred on the menu's top line

body.text: package.json's version is Peri's, a semantic one starting at 1.0.0, and it is bumped with every merge to main — AGENTS.md says how. Vite builds it into the bundle, so it is right offline, and the menu shows it at 0.8rem beside the name at 1.3rem, centred on the top line of every screen it shows.
The line is three columns now, and Back's is never narrower than Back: on a phone at a large text size the name gives way rather than the title being laid over the only way out.

commits.subject: Call it Peri, driven by pointing and dwell

body.text: The page title, the link preview, the installed app's name and the sign-in tagline all say the same thing now: Peri, and pointing rather than gaze — the board answers to any pointer that can rest, not only an eye tracker.

commits.subject: Carry the word lists in the spreadsheet, and give Backup the whole screen

body.text: The lists from Aliases ride after the phrases, one word a row, under the list's name in curly brackets and with no ID. Bringing a sheet back adds words and never takes one away; replacing makes each list hold the sheet's words and takes off the lists it leaves out, only where the sheet has any.
Backup & sharing fills the viewport as Settings and the guide do: held to half the screen, the spreadsheet's controls sat a dozen dwells below a panel that stopped halfway down.

commits.subject: Import and export the board as a spreadsheet: Excel, CSV and Google Sheets

body.text: Backup & sharing hands out the whole board as a spreadsheet and takes one back, for whoever helps somebody set their board up: writing two hundred phrases is an afternoon in Excel and a week by dwell.

One row a phrase — Category, Phrase, ID — the emergency bar first, then the tabs in order, each in its own arrangement. The phrase is its source, slots and markup and all. The ID is what makes the sheet an editor rather than a list, written with a # in front because a spreadsheet opening a base-36 id like 12e45 reads a number.

Three ways out: Save for Excel (a workbook whose cells are all text, the one to edit in Excel, which reads a CSV by guessing that 1/2 is a date), Save as CSV (with a byte-order mark, or Excel mangles every accent), and Copy for Sheets (tab-separated, pasted into an empty Google Sheet). Two back in: Choose a spreadsheet, which reads a workbook or text in UTF-8, Windows-1252 or UTF-16 and refuses a binary file, and Paste from Sheets.

Nothing changes before Peri says what will. Add and update adds new rows, rewords and moves rows whose ID matches, brings back a phrase taken off the board, finds rows already there by wording as the editor does, and never removes. Replace all phrases makes the board match the sheet, only for a sheet with IDs, saying first how many phrases that removes. Nothing moves onto or off the emergency bar unless somebody wrote it.

Formulas are disarmed with an apostrophe in every format, since a board is a file people hand to each other; number-like cells only in the paste, which obeys the apostrophe where opening a CSV shows it. Both come off on the way in, and only in front of something they could have guarded.

The workbook is written by hand — a board is three columns of text — with a stored zip out and the browser's DecompressionStream in. A workbook it writes opens in openpyxl with warnings as errors, and it reads a fixture openpyxl wrote plus the shapes Excel writes, built with Node's zlib.

FileButton is now the one file chooser, shared by the backup and the sheet, so a rest being refused by the browser is handled in one place. phraseKey and newPhraseId move into the store so the import and the editor agree about what is already on the board.

commits.subject: Keep the answers last offered across a reload, by the day's rules

body.text: The most recent answers already stayed on the board until newer ones replaced them, but only until the page reloaded — and a board on a mounted device is reloaded by whoever charges it rather than by the person using it, so answers that went with every reload went at somebody else's say-so.

They are written down on this device now, under peri_answers, as the words they were written in with the question they answered and when they arrived. The day's rules, because they are the day's conversation: forgotten after the same day the questions are, forgotten with them, never in a backup or a snapshot, cleared by a factory reset.

The day is enforced on the screen as well as in storage: reading back drops a record a day old, and a timer takes the answers off a board that never reloads when their day is up. Nothing is restored without a key, and the render that sees the key go takes the answers off the board, including a key removed on another device.

"Forget today's conversation" is the screen's to do now rather than the Settings row's: the row emptied storage by itself, which would have left the answers standing on the board until the next reload.

The privacy policy said an answer you did not choose is not kept, which is no longer true. It, the guide and the Settings row now say what is: the last answers offered are kept, and of the answers only the ones chosen are ever sent anywhere. The policy also called the control "the microphone button", which it stopped looking like in the last change.

commits.subject: Keep the most recent answers until newer ones replace them

body.text: Listening again, correcting the question and closing the box each cleared the answers, on the grounds that answers to a question no longer on screen might be taken for answers to the one that is. What that cost was the answers themselves: gone the moment the next person spoke or the box was put away, when somebody may well have wanted to go back to one.

So the most recent answers stay, under the Answers tab, until a new set replaces them. The risk the clearing guarded against is real in one window, and that window is covered: while newer answers are being asked for the tab shows the waiting line and none of the old ones, and a request that fails puts them straight back, being still the most recent there are.
The question a kept answer is written down against is named only when its answers arrive, so a choice made after a failed request goes into the conversation as the answer to the question it answered.

The board goes to the answers when a question goes off to be answered rather than whenever there are some — those outlast the question now, and opening the box again must not take the board to answers nobody is waiting for. It comes back when the box closes, or when asking brought nothing and nothing was kept. The answers landing hold the dwells in an effect of their own, since they no longer ride on the tab switching.

A correction clears the in-flight request's waiting line too. It always abandoned the request, and the line stood promising answers that never came — which would now also have hidden the kept ones behind it.

commits.subject: Draw the question control as a question mark, and say what each box takes

body.text: The control that opens the box above the message was a microphone, which says how the words arrive rather than what they are — and they do not only arrive that way: the box takes a question typed as readily as one heard. So it is a question mark now, drawn in the icon family's stroke with a filled dot, and the guide's :listen: mark draws the same one; a test holds the two to one picture, a guide that names a button having to show it.

The box waiting on it says "Speak or type a question" rather than "Listening…", which told somebody who cannot speak to it nothing about the half of it they could use. Once the recogniser stops it still says "Nothing heard yet", nothing being there to hear any more.
The message box, empty in auto-speak, says "Immediately speak selected phrase" — what a dwell on a phrase will do — rather than describing the mode by what it does not do.

commits.subject: Let each mode toggle mean its own mode, and listen in auto-speak

body.text: The two toggles sat in a ring: switching auto-speak off landed in edit mode, on the grounds that somebody who does not want a phrase spoken must want to change it. So the one control a person building a sentence reaches for put them in the one mode where a dwell rewrites the board, and composing — what they were after — was a second dwell away on the other control. The pair furthest apart in the ring was the pair used most.

Switching one on still switches the other off, speaking and rewording asking opposite things of the same dwell. Switching one off now leaves the other alone, so each of the three states is one dwell from the other two and neither control ever does nothing.

Opening the microphone puts the board in auto-speak. Somebody has just been spoken to and is about to answer with a person waiting in front of them, which is the whole of what auto-speak is for; the alternative is a board that hears a question and then wants a second dwell somewhere else before it can say anything back. Only on the way in — a conversation that has ended is no reason to stop talking — and it says nothing when the board was already talking, a toast about a change nobody made being something that aims a gaze rather than merely distracting it.

The rule lives beside setMode in talk.tsx, so the microphone control takes an onToggleListen from the screen rather than calling listener.toggle straight: the hook knows about microphones and nothing about modes.
